The mass dimension of the coupling constant \(\kappa\) is determined by requiring the action to be dimensionless. In 4 spacetime dimensions, the Lagrangian density has mass dimension 4. The fermion fields \(\psi\) and \(\bar{\psi}\) each have mass dimension \(3/2\), the field strength tensor \(F^{\mu\nu}\) has mass dimension 2, and \(\sigma_{\mu\nu}\) is dimensionless. Thus, the operator \(\bar{\psi}\sigma_{\mu\nu}\psi F^{\mu\nu}\) has mass dimension \(3/2 + 3/2 + 2 = 5\). For \(\mathcal{L}_{int}\) to have mass dimension 4, \(\kappa\) must have mass dimension \(-1\).

A theory is renormalizable by power counting if all coupling constants have mass dimension \(\ge 0\). Since \([\kappa] = -1\), the interaction is non-renormalizable.

Answer: D
